with_skill.expectation: Advises topic titles written in the asker's own words, because title and first post become the search snippet
Assigns a daily pass on unanswered or unsolved topics to a named owner
Recommends a separate Announcements category for release posts
Does not decide the Discord-versus-Discourse switch itself

without_skill.expectation: Requires the original asker's consent (or anonymised rewriting with consent) before a ticket becomes a public topic
Recommends a Categories homepage (rather than Latest) while the forum is young
Gives a dated cadence that works back from the Nov 21 opening (pre-launch weeks, launch week, first 90 days)
Assigns a named owner or rota for a daily pass on unanswered topics during the first 90 days
Notes that links from TL3 posts lose nofollow by default, so bulk TL3 rewards link spammers
Cites at least one concrete TL0 default limit (for example 3 topics and 10 replies on day one, 2 links, or no attachments)
Places raising TL1 requirements after faster controls (spam detection, watched words, TL0-only queue), noting day-one spam posts as TL0
Recommends capping new accounts per IP address (default 3)
Allows at most TL1 for verified customers (for example through a group) and leaves higher levels to be earned or granted individually
Labels platform defaults as Discourse defaults that the admin can change or should verify in settings
Notes Discourse recommends a subdomain, or that a subfolder requires maintaining robots.txt at the root by hand
Suggests auditing the crawler view of a topic (for example with ?print or the crawler header)
Suggests checking that solved topics are public, canonical and present in the sitemap
Advises topic titles written in the asker's own words, because title and first post become the search snippet
Labels claims by source (Google versus Discourse versus practitioner) rather than presenting all as fact
Recommends Solved and the unsolved filter as the triage queue for support topics
Proposes growing non-staff helpers through trust levels, and promoting proven helpers to TL4 by hand
Sets a time-to-first-reply target (for example a median under 24 hours)
Names Discourse admin reports (time to first response, topics with no response, trust level growth) as the data source
Includes a stop or fold-back rule if non-staff solutions and TL2 growth do not move
Recommends a separate Announcements category for release posts
Says Announcements can be excluded from the summary email with its suppress-categories setting
Routes the single-sign-on and docs-embedding work to samber/developer-platform-skills@developer-portal-design
Routes the forum-versus-Discord venue decision to samber/developer-relations-skills@developer-community-launch
Does not write DiscourseConnect or embed configuration steps itself
Does not decide the Discord-versus-Discourse switch itself
Offers to continue with forum operations (categories, trust levels, seeding or SEO) once those are settled
